clue.text: Flipping Tarzan's right for the title role

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it end to end, so the word for Tarzan is read from its back

parts.note: Tarzan is the ape man, raised by apes in the jungle; the 's is 'Tarzan is'
RT is a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Tarzan's turning out fine for the lead in a film is described as a flip.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarzan's = Tarzan is APE MAN; flipped it gives NAMEPA, and RT completes NAME PART.
explanation.definitionFit: A name part is a role whose character gives the play or film its name, like Hamlet or Tarzan himself.

clue.text: Supporter upset New York players

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting something tips it over so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the Mets are a New York baseball team

explanation.surface: A fan is upset by the performance of a New York team.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's stalk holds up the flower or leaves, so it is literally a physical support.

clue.text: Quarrel with composer about second note of major scale

indicators.note: about means around, so the composer's name goes round the note

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer
in sol-fa the major scale runs do, re, mi, so re is the second

explanation.surface: A row with a composer over the second note of a scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a rift or falling-out between people, the result of a serious disagreement.

clue.text: Mother, close to ground, heard playwright

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken as spoken, so we want something sounding like them

parts.note: Mother is MA and close to the ground is LOW; said together in a non-rhotic accent they make the name

explanation.surface: A mother lying near the ground overheard a dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan dramatist who wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine.

clue.text: Lanky Scots go on heather

parts.note: gang is the Scottish verb meaning to go
ling is the common heather

explanation.surface: Tall thin Scotsmen go walking on the heather of the moors.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts GANG above LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and awkward in movement, much the same as lanky.

clue.text: Remove dairy produce before getting exasperated

parts.note: cheese is a dairy product
to doff is to take off, as a hat

explanation.surface: Someone clears away the cheese before losing their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' comes first in the clue but its word goes after the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesed off is British slang for annoyed, fed up or irritated beyond patience.

clue.text: French language for British school

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for British
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: French as a subject for a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is the Celtic tongue spoken in Brittany, a language of France though not French itself.

clue.text: Microscopic organisms evidently originating in part of central Asia

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the region named after it

parts.note: Bactria was an ancient region of central Asia, roughly modern Afghanistan

indicators.note: where a word originates is its start, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of evidently

explanation.surface: Germs apparently first came from a corner of central Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacteria are single-celled microbes, far too small to see without a microscope.

clue.text: A horse at sea and on land

indicators.note: at sea means confused and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A horse that swims at sea and then walks on land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets sea against land; 'at sea' is really the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on the beach or dry ground rather than on the water.

clue.text: Island recluse is not with it

indicators.note: is not with says something is taken away, leaving the word without it

parts.note: a hermit lives alone, cut off from society
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A loner on an island is out of touch with fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, lying near Guernsey between England and France.

clue.text: Everyone, say, backed animal movement

parts.note: everyone means all
e.g. means for example, as does say

indicators.note: backed means going backwards, so the animal's name is read from its end

parts.note: the otter is a river animal

explanation.surface: Everyone supported a campaign for animal welfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' looks like a cause; it is a section of a musical work. OTTER reversed gives RETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegretto is a fairly brisk piece or section of a symphony or sonata, so a musical movement.

clue.text: Like Hamlet and his rotten state

definitions.text: Like Hamlet and his rotten state

parts.words: Like Hamlet and his rotten state
parts.note: surface: a description of a gloomy prince and his corrupt country

parts.words: Like Hamlet and his rotten state
parts.note: setter's reading: Hamlet was Prince of Denmark, and 'something is rotten in the state of Denmark', so both share a nationality

explanation.walkthrough: Marcellus says 'Something is rotten in the state of Denmark' in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for Denmark and its people describes both the prince and the kingdom he lived in.

clue.text: Corpse isn't laid out for police officers

indicators.note: laid out means arranged afresh, so the letters are set out in another order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A body still awaiting the undertaker, ready for the detectives to examine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' suggests a body prepared for burial, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector is a rank in the British police, above sergeant, so inspectors are senior officers.

clue.text: Insect entangled with a net

indicators.note: something entangled is twisted and knotted together, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bug caught up in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: White ant is the popular name for the termite, a wood-eating social insect.

clue.text: A disposable hanky under discussion

parts.note: taken as written
a paper tissue is a throwaway handkerchief

explanation.surface: A paper handkerchief being talked about.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter at issue is the point being debated or disputed at the moment.

clue.text: Dour poet shaken and dragged out of bed?

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled about, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A grim poet is rattled after being hauled out of bed in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a sleeper's; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant pulled up roots and all from the garden border has been removed from its flower bed.

clue.text: Shunned revolutionary soldier not a communist

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the soldier is read backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
no is a word of refusal, like not
a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: A rebel fighter was cold-shouldered for not being a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' and 'communist' together paint politics, but the first only turns GI round.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to snub them, deliberately paying them no attention.

clue.text: Upstanding French maid was first elevated

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: bonne is French for a maidservant
to have led is to have been in front

explanation.surface: An honest French maid was the first to be promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being raised to the peerage is an elevation in rank, making someone a noble.

clue.text: Smart case for a tool

indicators.note: a case holds something inside, so the first word wraps round the next

parts.note: smart means clever
taken as written

explanation.surface: A neat box to keep a tool in.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleaver is a heavy broad-bladed chopper used by butchers.

clue.text: Two-faced male doctor has external face

indicators.note: having something external means being wrapped from outside, so the face goes round

parts.note: dial is slang for face, and the face of a clock
he is the male pronoun
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A deceitful male doctor whose face shows nothing inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-faced' looks like deceit, but here it is geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A dihedral angle is formed by two intersecting planes, so the word means having two flat surfaces.

clue.text: One South American country ejecting unknown reptile

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: ejecting means throwing out, so one letter is removed from the country

parts.note: Guyana is on the north coast of South America
algebra's unknowns are x, y and z

explanation.surface: A South American nation deports a mysterious lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, and lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Doting on gold, basically

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another sits after it, so the doting word is placed second

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
fond means doting, loving

explanation.surface: Someone besotted with gold, essentially a miser.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a French phrase borrowed into English; the surface's miser is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Au fond is a French phrase used in English meaning at bottom, fundamentally.

clue.text: A release from the BBC?

parts.note: taken as written
to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A press release or broadcast issued by the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC, Britain's public broadcaster, is nicknamed Auntie, or Auntie Beeb.
explanation.definitionFit: The affectionate nickname for the British Broadcasting Corporation stands for the corporation itself.

clue.text: Robin and Tuck with a wild rock star

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Robin Hood and Friar Tuck run off with a wild rocker.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin and Tuck call up Sherwood Forest's outlaws, but they are only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Cobain was the singer and guitarist of the grunge band Nirvana.

clue.text: Bishop has talk about talks

indicators.note: the talk has the bishop, holding it within itself
about means around, so the talk word goes round the bishop

parts.note: gas is idle talk or chatter
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop chats about his speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: To gab is to chatter at length, so it gabs means it talks idly.

clue.text: Tennis player gaining recognition after false starts

indicators.note: starts are the opening letters, so only the first of each word is used

parts.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A tennis player becomes famous after several false starts in her career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False starts' sounds like a sprint, but it marks the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf is the German tennis champion who won all four majors and Olympic gold in 1988.

clue.text: Utterly nasty tribal leaders regret being false

indicators.note: leaders are those in front, so only each word's opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Cruel tribal chiefs are sorry for telling lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means not correct, the same as a false statement.

clue.text: Times are changing for some Arab lands

indicators.note: changing means altering their arrangement, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Change is coming to parts of the Arab world.
explanation.definitionFit: Emirates are states ruled by an emir, such as those forming the United Arab Emirates.
